en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Fourth Chapter
The Discourse on the Marks:
Is it the case that a Bodhisatta is one endowed with the marks?
Yes, he is.
Is one who possesses the partial characteristics a partial bodhisatta?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is a bodhisatta one who possesses the [full] characteristics?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is one who possesses the characteristics of three parts a ‘three-part bodhisattva’?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is one who possesses all the marks a Bodhisatta? Yes.
Is one who possesses half the marks half a Bodhisatta? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one endowed with the characteristics a Bodhisatta? Yes.
"A wheel-turning monarch possesses the marks; a wheel-turning monarch is a Bodhisatta"?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
"A wheel-turning monarch possesses the marks; a wheel-turning monarch is a Bodhisatta"? One should not say so.
“Yes,” you say.

“Is the former application, the former conduct, the proclamation of the Dhamma, and the teaching of the Dhamma of a Bodhisatta the same as the former application, the former conduct, the proclamation of the Dhamma, and the teaching of the Dhamma of a Wheel-turning Monarch (cakkavatti-satta)?
You must not say so… [and so on].
"Just as when a Bodhisatta is born, the gods receive him first and humans afterwards, so too, when a Wheel-turning Monarch is born, the gods receive him first and humans afterwards"?
One should not say this... [and so on]...
"Just as when a Bodhisatta is born, four sons of the gods receive him and place him before his mother"?
“Be joyful, O Queen;
a son of great power has been born to you. In the same way, when the being destined to be a wheel-turning monarch is born, four sons of gods receive him and place him before his mother, saying:
“Be joyful, O Queen.”
“Has a son of great power been born to you?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Just as when the Bodhisatta was being born, two streams of water appeared from the sky— one of cool water and one of warm water— to bathe him.
One [stream] was cool and one was warm—
by which they performed the water-rites for the Bodhisatta and his mother; in the same way, when a Wheel-turning Monarch is being born, two streams of water appear from the sky—
one cool and one warm.
And by what means do they perform the water-rites for the Wheel-turning Monarch and for his mother?
One must not say so...
[as before] ...Just as the Bodhisatta, immediately upon birth, stood with even feet, facing north, and took seven strides.
As he walks while a white parasol is held over him, he surveys all directions and utters a lion’s roar:
"I am the foremost in the world; I am the eldest in the world; I am the best in the world. This is my final birth;
there is now no further existence. Even so, as soon as he is born, the being who is to be a Wheel-turning Monarch stands firmly with his feet level upon the ground.
Why does he proceed facing north with a stride of seven steps while a white parasol is held over him;
why does he survey all directions and utter this lion’s roar:
“I am the foremost in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the best in the world; this is the final birth, now there is no more renewed existence”?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Just as there is the manifestation of great light, great radiance, and a great earthquake when the Bodhisatta is being born,
even so there is the manifestation of great light and great radiance when a Wheel-turning Monarch is being born.
Is there the manifestation of a great earthquake?

One should not say so… [as before]… Just as the natural body of a Bodhisatta radiates light for a fathom all around, is it likewise the case that the natural body of a Wheel-turning Monarch radiates light for a fathom all around?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Just as the Bodhisatta sees a great dream, so too does the Cakkavatti-satta see a great dream?
It should not be said thus … [as before].
Is it not to be said that “the Bodhisatta is endowed with the marks”?
Yes, it is.
"Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
'Bhikkhus, there are these thirty-two marks of a Great Man possessed by which a Great Man has only two possible destinies and no other.
If he lives the life of a householder, he becomes a Wheel-turning Monarch, righteous, a king of Dharma, conqueror of the four quarters, stabilizer of the land, endowed with the seven treasures. ..."
He possesses these seven treasures, namely:
the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the jewel-treasure, the woman-treasure, the householder-treasure, and the counselor-treasure as the seventh.
Furthermore, he has more than a thousand sons who are brave, heroic in form, and crushers of enemy armies.
Thus he dwells having conquered this earth, bounded by the ocean, without rod or sword, by means of the Dhamma.
But if he goes forth from the home life into homelessness, he becomes an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One who has drawn back the veil from the world.
Is there such a sutta?
“Yes, [they do].
“In that case, a Bodhisatta is one who is endowed with the marks.
The Discussion on the Marks is finished.
